follow-up time: 24 months (from vaccination at 18 months to antibody measurement at 36 months)
exposure: mode of delivery (cesarean section vs vaginal delivery)
outcome: measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine-induced antibody titers at 36 months of age
cohort: Children from the FARMFLORA birth cohort, including both farming and non-farming families, immunized with the MMR vaccine at 18 months of age
finding: Delayed adaptive immune maturation before and close to MMR immunization, female sex, and cesarean section birth were associated with higher anti-MMR antibody titers at 36 months of age.
mod_finding: Children born by cesarean section had significantly higher anti-measles titers than vaginally-born children.
